functions.funcDef: Convert bus energy into shaft power at the propellers and modulate it to command (§2.1 PRL/PRR are Function-type; §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Left propulsion unit converts bus energy to shaft power at the left propeller and modulates to thrust command (§5.1.1). Independent means: own inverter, own nacelle, channel-1 control (§5.1.4/5.1.5).

functions.funcDef: Convert bus energy into shaft power at the propellers and modulate it to command (§2.1 PRL/PRR are Function-type; §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Right propulsion unit converts bus energy to shaft power at the right propeller and modulates to thrust command (§5.2.1). Installation-independent of left: run B, channel 2, opposite nacelle (§5.2.5).

functions.funcDef: Command and monitor primary and secondary control-surface positions in response to crew and autopilot inputs (§5.6.1/5.7.1).
functions.subName: Command primary control surfaces via channel A
functions.subDef: Channel A commands elevator/aileron halves and upper rudder segment and monitors response (§5.6.1/5.6.2). Independent channel: channel-1 power, primary sensors, team-1 processing (§5.6.5).

functions.funcDef: Command and monitor primary and secondary control-surface positions in response to crew and autopilot inputs (§5.6.1/5.7.1).
functions.subName: Command primary control surfaces via channel B
functions.subDef: Channel B commands the other surface halves and lower rudder segment and monitors response (§5.7.1/5.7.2). Dissimilar channel: channel-2 power, standby sensors, team-2 processing (§5.7.2/5.7.5).

functions.funcDef: Command and monitor primary and secondary control-surface positions in response to crew and autopilot inputs (§5.6.1/5.7.1).
functions.subName: Provide secondary flight control (flap and pitch trim)
functions.subDef: Flap drive and pitch trim commanded by whichever channel is in control, with asymmetry braking per flap section (§5.6.2). Mechanical reversion retained to pitch trim and lower rudder (§5.6.3).

functions.funcDef: Present attitude, air data, powertrain state and warnings to the crew, and supply sensed data to the flight control channels (§5.10.1/5.11.1).
functions.subName: Provide primary flight and powertrain display
functions.subDef: Primary display presents attitude, air data, powertrain state and prioritised crew alerting, and supplies sensed data to channel A (§5.10.1/5.10.2). On primary sensor set and channel 1 (§5.10.5).

functions.funcDef: Present attitude, air data, powertrain state and warnings to the crew, and supply sensed data to the flight control channels (§5.10.1/5.11.1).
functions.subName: Provide standby attitude and air-data indication
functions.subDef: Standby display presents attitude and air data on independent source and supply, and supplies sensed data to channel B (§5.11.1). Independent across sensor, probe, channel and battery (§5.11.3).

functions.funcDef: Extend, retract, seal and indicate a retractable tricycle gear appropriate to the selected landing surface (§5.14.1).
functions.subName: Actuate and stow the landing gear
functions.subDef: Electro-mechanical extension/retraction of nose and main units with mechanical free-fall backstop, power split across both channels (§5.14.2/5.14.3). No hydraulic system on the aircraft (§5.14.2).

functions.funcDef: Extend, retract, seal and indicate a retractable tricycle gear appropriate to the selected landing surface (§5.14.1).
functions.subName: Indicate gear configuration against selected surface
functions.subDef: Two dissimilar position sensors per lock compared and annunciated as a mismatch against the crew's surface selection (§5.14.2/5.14.6). Surface selection is an explicit crew input (§5.14.6).

functions.funcName: Provide directional control on the water
functions.funcDef: Provide steering during water operations (§5.13.1 "provides directional control on the water") — a behaviour, distinct from the hull's structural integrity.
functions.subDef: Retractable water rudder driven by its own actuator and steered from the pedals, with revert-to-differential-thrust on actuator loss (§5.13.2/5.13.3). Gear-down retraction interlock hardwired (§5.13.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire, overheat and thermal-runaway in fire zones and cabin, contain or isolate, and give the crew means to discharge (§5.15.1).
functions.subName: Detect fire, overheat and thermal-runaway conditions
functions.subDef: Dual-loop detection per fire zone plus store-bay module thermal sensing, and photoelectric cabin/baggage smoke detection (§5.15.2). Loops on separate channels/routes (§5.15.5).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire, overheat and thermal-runaway in fire zones and cabin, contain or isolate, and give the crew means to discharge (§5.15.1).
functions.subName: Contain, isolate or extinguish a detected event
functions.subDef: Store-bay containment via enclosure/overboard vent, nacelle isolation via contactor-open and feather, generator-bay extinguishant bottle (§5.15.2). Suppression is not redundant (§5.15.3).

functions.funcDef: Maintain habitable cabin pressure, temperature and ventilation through the mission and clear the windscreen (§5.16.1).
functions.subDef: Bleed-fed air-cycle pack with single outflow and independent relief valve; electrical recirc/heat reversion provides unpressurised ventilation on generator shutdown (§5.16.2/5.16.3).

functions.funcDef: Maintain habitable cabin pressure, temperature and ventilation through the mission and clear the windscreen (§5.16.1).
functions.subDef: Windscreen anti-fog, bleed-fed with an electric backup element (§5.16.2). Distinct output of the ECS from cabin conditioning (§5.16.1).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded left-side thrust (thrust applied or changed on the left unit without a crew or control-channel command)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust on one side produces a thrust asymmetry the opposing unit does not match, generating a yawing and rolling moment the flight-control channels and crew must counter. On the water an uncommanded thrust change degrades directional control during taxi. The aircraft remains controllable through the flight-control surfaces and by retarding/feathering the affected unit, but a large reduction in safety margins occurs during take-off/initial climb where speed and control authority are lowest.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the asymmetry, apply corrective control, and retard or feather the affected unit; single-lever-per-side thrust and guarded feather are available. Significant increase in workload during the recovery, greatest at low speed/low altitude.
fha.effPax: Transient upset (yaw/roll) during the excursion; no injury expected if control is recovered promptly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded thrust asymmetry at low speed on take-off/initial climb yields a large reduction in safety margins with high compensating workload; opposing unit and feather path preserve controllability short of catastrophic. Worst-phase (take-off) drives the class. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous left-side thrust response — asymmetric (left unit delivers thrust materially different from that commanded, producing an asymmetry against the right unit)
fha.effAc: Erroneous (too-high or too-low) thrust on the left unit relative to command creates a lateral thrust asymmetry against the right unit, requiring surface trim and possibly feathering of the affected unit; controllable through the flight-control channels and the opposing unit, with the largest margin reduction at low-speed phases.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the anomaly from powertrain indication and aircraft response, trim against the asymmetry and feather the affected unit if required; significant workload increase during recovery.
fha.effPax: Transient lateral upset; no injury expected with prompt recovery.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detected asymmetric erroneous thrust at low speed drives a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload; opposing unit and feather preserve controllability. Take-off phase is worst case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous left-side thrust response — undetected (left unit delivers thrust different from commanded with the crew unaware, continuing normal duties and taking no corrective action)
fha.effAc: With the erroneous thrust undetected, the asymmetry is uncorrected: the flight-control channels trim residually but the crew does not feather or retard the affected unit. Sustained uncorrected asymmetry at low speed erodes controllability toward a large-to-severe reduction in safety margins, particularly on take-off/initial climb.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; no corrective feather/trim initiated until the aircraft response itself forces recognition, by which point control margin may be substantially reduced.
fha.effPax: Sustained lateral upset; potential for injury if control margin is exceeded before recognition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a committed class: the outcome of an UNDETECTED erroneous-thrust asymmetry depends on how large a mis-thrust the flight-control channels absorb before controllability is threatened and on the time-to-annunciation, neither of which the SDD quantifies. Needs the control-law asymmetry-rejection authority and the detection/annunciation coverage of an erroneous (non-locked-rotor) thrust to determine whether the undetected case reaches Hazardous or Catastrophic.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of left-side thrust (left unit produces reduced thrust; crew aware)
fha.effAc: Reduced thrust on one unit is the sizing case for the pair: the aircraft continues the sector on the opposing unit's rating with the affected side derated or feathered. A thrust asymmetry must be trimmed; safety margins are reduced but the aircraft remains controllable and able to continue or divert.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe the derate/reduced power on the powertrain page, manage the asymmetry and, if a locked rotor or unusable output, feather the affected unit for the remaining unit's rating; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Minor discomfort from reduced performance and trim change; no injury expected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss of one of two units is the declared continuation case, giving a significant (not large) reduction in performance and safety margins with a significant increase in crew workload; the aircraft continues on the opposing unit. Take-off/climb is worst case. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of left-side thrust — undetected (left unit output reduced with the crew unaware, continuing normal duties and taking no action)
fha.effAc: With the reduced thrust undetected, the affected side is not derated-managed or feathered and the residual asymmetry is left to the flight-control channels; a windmilling or unfeathered under-performing unit degrades the remaining-unit rating case the SDD relies on, reducing continuation performance and control margin, most acutely at low speed.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; the reduced-thrust condition is not managed and the feather-for-rating action the sizing case assumes is not taken.
fha.effPax: Reduced performance and asymmetry; no immediate injury expected if recognised before an approach/climb margin is exhausted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a committed class: the continuation-case rating in the SDD explicitly assumes the failed side is feathered ('a windmilling propeller on the failed side has to be feathered for the remaining unit's rating to be sufficient'); whether an UNDETECTED partial loss with no feather still permits continuation, and the annunciation coverage of a partial (not total) thrust loss, are not quantified. Needs the detection/annunciation coverage for a partial thrust shortfall and the remaining-unit rating with the affected propeller unfeathered.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of left-side thrust
fha.effAc: Aircraft is left with a single propulsion unit and an asymmetric-thrust condition; the failed-side propeller must be feathered for the remaining unit's rating to be sufficient to continue the sector. Continuation on the remaining unit is the pair sizing case per the SDD. Directional trim required to counter yaw; reduced climb/performance margins, worst at take-off/climb weight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must identify the failed side, feather the failed propeller and re-trim for asymmetric flight; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: No direct injury from the condition itself; continued safe flight and landing achievable on the remaining unit.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in performance/climb margins and asymmetric-thrust handling in a twin, with the remaining unit sized to continue only after correct feathering; worst-case at take-off/climb. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded right-side thrust
fha.effAc: Thrust on the right side not matching the crew command produces an asymmetric-thrust and yawing condition; the two thrust levers are mechanically independent and not ganged, so the crew command and delivered thrust can diverge on one side. Uncommanded change in one-side thrust perturbs trajectory and asymmetry, worst near the ground where control margins and reaction time are least.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded thrust, counter the resulting yaw, and manage/feather the affected unit; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: No direct injury assumed if the crew counters the asymmetry; safe continuation depends on timely crew response.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support an asymmetric-thrust/yaw upset, but the magnitude and reversibility of an uncommanded right-side thrust excursion (transient vs. sustained, and whether it drives loss of control near the ground) are not established in the provided function definition; classification requires that severity input before committing between Major and Catastrophic.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous right-side thrust response — asymmetric
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — No FCIM condition SF-002-M2 exists in the project state for SF-002 (the listed malfunctions are SF-002-M and SF-002-M3); there is no grounded condition text or effect to classify. Row emitted per turn scope but abstains on all effect and severity fields pending confirmation of what, if anything, this id refers to.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous right-side thrust response — undetected
fha.effAc: Right-side thrust differs from intended with the crew unaware, so no corrective feathering or re-trim is taken; the asymmetry/yaw is allowed to develop unopposed. With the crew continuing normal duties, the trajectory deviation accumulates rather than being arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding the condition (unaware case); no crew mitigation credited.
fha.effPax: Exposure to an uncorrected asymmetric-thrust deviation; occupant outcome depends on how far the deviation develops before it becomes evident.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An undetected erroneous thrust response removes the crew mitigation credited elsewhere, so severity should be no better than the aware malfunction — but the aircraft outcome of an unopposed right-side thrust error (does it progress to loss of control) is not quantified in the provided function definition; committing between Hazardous and Catastrophic requires that input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of right-side thrust
fha.effAc: Right side produces reduced thrust; a mild asymmetric-thrust condition with reduced total available power and reduced performance margins. Depending on magnitude the unit may be derated rather than lost; the pair-level continuation case assumes a full unit loss, so a partial loss leaves more than the single-unit case but with a standing asymmetry to trim.
fha.effCrew: Crew re-trim for the residual asymmetry and manage power/derate; moderate increase in workload.
fha.effPax: No direct injury assumed; continued safe flight with reduced margins.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in performance/functional capability and a standing asymmetry requiring crew re-trim, short of the large-reduction/single-unit case; worst near take-off/climb. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of right-side thrust — undetected (crew continue normally, no thrust rebalance or feather action taken)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust with reduced right-side power that is not annunciated; aircraft develops an uncorrected yaw/roll tendency and reduced total thrust margin that the crew do not compensate for because the degradation is undetected. Twin wing-mounted units means the asymmetry is a directional-control and performance-margin item.
fha.effCrew: No alert presented; crew fly the aircraft trimming out an unexplained asymmetry, with increased workload if the trend continues to a point where the handling cue becomes noticeable.
fha.effPax: No direct effect unless the asymmetry progresses.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the pair is sized so a coastal sector continues after loss of one unit, but does not quantify how much thrust is lost in a 'partial' undetected case, at which phase the reduced margin bites, or the resulting handling/performance envelope — so the aircraft effect cannot be resolved to a single class without engineering data on partial-loss magnitude and its take-off/climb performance consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of right-side thrust
fha.effAc: Total loss of thrust from the right unit leaves the aircraft on the left unit alone. The SDD sizing case is continuation of a coastal sector on one unit with the failed-side propeller feathered; a windmilling propeller on the failed side must be feathered for the remaining unit's rating to suffice. Asymmetric thrust demands directional-control input; total-thrust margin is reduced, most critical at take-off/climb and go-around.
fha.effCrew: Failure is annunciated (aware condition); crew feather the failed unit and manage asymmetry and reduced climb performance, with increased workload during the phase of loss.
fha.effPax: No injury expected if the single-unit continuation case holds; increased crew activity and possible diversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Stated effects are a significant reduction in performance margin and functional capability (one of two thrust sources lost) with continued safe flight on the remaining unit per the SDD sizing case, at increased crew workload — a significant, not large, reduction in safety margins. Contingent on the single-unit continuation and feather assumptions holding across take-off/go-around; if single-unit climb performance is inadequate in a critical phase this escalates. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary surface command (channel A commands a surface position different from that intended; crew aware via monitored cross-compare disagreement and channel transfer)
fha.effAc: Channel A issues an erroneous command to its half of a surface pair. Per the SDD the two channels cross-compare surface position and transfer is automatic on a monitored disagreement and annunciated; each channel alone can fly the aircraft through its own half of each surface pair. The erroneous command produces a transient surface deviation until the monitored transfer isolates channel A, after which control is retained on channel B.
fha.effCrew: Disagreement is annunciated and transfer is automatic; crew manage a degraded-law reversion and the transient, at increased workload.
fha.effPax: Transient upset possible before transfer; no injury expected if transfer is prompt.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the monitored cross-compare and automatic annunciated transfer stated in the SDD, the erroneous command is detected and isolated with control retained on the dissimilar channel — a significant reduction in margins and a significant workload increase during the transient/reversion, not a large reduction. Contingent on the cross-compare detecting the specific erroneous command and transfer authority being sufficient before the transient becomes hazardous. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded primary surface motion (surface moves without a corresponding channel command)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition (SF-003-M2, 'Uncommanded primary surface motion') is not present in the SF-003 FCIM in the current project state, which carries only SF-003-M (erroneous, aware) and SF-003-M3 (erroneous, undetected). Without a distinct FCIM/function statement I cannot characterise how it differs from the erroneous-command condition or state an aircraft effect — confirm whether M2 is a real condition or a duplicate before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary surface command — undetected (channel A commands an erroneous surface position and the cross-compare monitor does not detect it; crew continue normally, no transfer occurs)
fha.effAc: An erroneous command that escapes the monitored cross-compare is not isolated by automatic transfer, so the erroneous surface deflection persists on channel A's half of the surface pair while the crew take no corrective channel action. Depending on surface, phase and magnitude this is an uncorrected flight-path deviation with the primary detection/isolation defence assumed defeated.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew do not initiate transfer and fly against an uncommanded/erroneous deflection they cannot attribute, with the mechanical reversion path (pitch trim and lower rudder only) as the residual.
fha.effPax: Uncorrected upset possible; injury potential depends on magnitude and phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The undetected case removes the monitored cross-compare/transfer defence the SDD relies on, but the SDD does not state the maximum authority or rate of an erroneous channel-A command, whether it is bounded by surface/actuator limits, or the controllability of the resulting deflection in the worst phase — so the aircraft effect could range from a recoverable deviation to a loss of control, and cannot be resolved to a single class without the erroneous-command authority/controllability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary surface command via channel B, undetected — channel B issues an incorrect surface command with the crew and the cross-compare monitor unaware, so no automatic transfer to channel A occurs
fha.effAc: An undetected erroneous command on channel B's half of a surface pair opposes the other half and produces an uncommanded, unmonitored control-surface deviation; because the fault is undetected the monitored cross-compare and automatic channel transfer do not act, so the erroneous input persists and can drive the aircraft toward a departure from controlled flight
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no annunciation (undetected); must recognise an unexplained trajectory divergence and manually diagnose and select the healthy channel, a high-workload recovery under adverse conditions
fha.effPax: Potential for injury from the resulting manoeuvre; outcome depends on phase and recovery
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes the surfaces are split half-per-channel and monitored by cross-compare with automatic transfer (§5.6.2/§5.6.3), but by definition this row is the DEFEAT of that monitor (undetected). Whether an undetected erroneous half-surface command is survivable (opposed by the healthy half) or drives loss of control depends on surface authority, control-law behaviour on an undetected disagreement, and phase — none of which the design description quantifies. Cannot derive a class without that; abstaining rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded primary surface motion via channel B, undetected — channel B drives one of its surface halves without pilot or autopilot command, with the cross-compare monitor unaware so no automatic transfer occurs
fha.effAc: An undetected uncommanded deflection of channel B's half of a surface (elevator inboard, aileron or lower rudder segment) introduces an unwanted moment opposed only by the healthy half of the pair; undetected, it defeats the monitored transfer and persists, degrading trajectory control
fha.effCrew: No annunciation; crew must detect an unexplained control disturbance and select the healthy channel manually — a high-workload, time-critical diagnosis
fha.effPax: Possible injury from the resulting manoeuvre depending on phase and recovery
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — NOTE: SF-004-M4 is not present in the SF-004 FCIM (the Unaware row carries only SF-004-M3) — this row has no matching FCIM cell in state and should be reconciled. Beyond that: as with SF-004-M3, the undetected case defeats the cross-compare/auto-transfer that the SDD relies on, and the design description does not quantify per-half surface authority, control-law response to an undetected disagreement, or phase dependence. The aircraft effect cannot be resolved to a class without that; abstaining.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous secondary flight control — flap drive or pitch trim commanded incorrectly (crew-aware)
fha.effAc: Erroneous secondary flight control (flap drive or pitch trim) — flaps are driven by a single power drive unit per function with asymmetry braking at each flap section, so an asymmetric flap event is arrested by the braking; erroneous pitch trim introduces an out-of-trim pitch moment the pilot must oppose. Effect on the aircraft ranges from an out-of-trim condition to an asymmetric-flap transient limited by the section braking; most consequential in take-off/approach/landing where flap and trim settings are configuration-critical
fha.effCrew: Detected/annunciated (crew-aware); crew respond by opposing/retrimming or reverting to the mechanical pitch-trim path, and by managing flap configuration — increased workload during a configuration-critical phase
fha.effPax: Possible discomfort from a trim transient; no direct injury expected in the aware, managed case
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD gives the secondary-control architecture (single PDU per function, asymmetry braking per flap section, mechanical reversion to pitch trim — §5.6.2/§5.6.3) but does not quantify the magnitude of an erroneous trim runaway or a braked asymmetric-flap transient, nor its effect on safety margins by phase. Whether the worst-case aware erroneous secondary control is Major (significant margin reduction at a configuration-critical phase) or Minor cannot be derived from the definition alone; abstaining rather than reaching for a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded secondary flight control — inadvertent flap or pitch-trim actuation not commanded by the crew
fha.effAc: Uncommanded flap movement or trim runaway changes the aircraft pitch attitude and configuration away from the selected state; flap asymmetry is limited by section asymmetry braking, and a trim runaway is opposed by the crew through the primary controls until arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the attitude/configuration change against the intended state, arrest the runaway (isolate trim / stop flap drive) and re-establish the flight path; workload rises significantly during the recovery.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded secondary control produces a recoverable attitude/configuration excursion with a significant increase in crew workload to arrest and correct it; asymmetry braking bounds the flap case. Passenger effect not grounded by the function definition. Confirm against control-authority and trim-rate data. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch trim — undetected: pitch trim set to an incorrect position without crew awareness, crew continuing normal duties
fha.effAc: An erroneous, undetected trim position leaves the aircraft trimmed away from the required condition; at a configuration change (take-off rotation, approach) the mistrim produces an out-of-trim pitching moment the crew must overcome, reducing pitch safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action for the trim itself; they encounter unexpected control forces at the critical phase and must react without prior awareness.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity of an undetected mistrim turns on the available trim authority and the phase at which it manifests — a large mistrim at rotation or on approach could be a large reduction in safety margins, a small one only significant. The AFHA function set fixes neither the trim authority nor the detection means, so the aircraft effect cannot be bounded to one class without that data; abstaining rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch trim — undetected: trim drives away from the set position without command and without crew awareness, crew continuing normal duties
fha.effAc: An undetected uncommanded trim excursion progressively mistrims the aircraft; with no crew action the out-of-trim pitching moment grows until it is arrested by trim travel limits or overcomes available pitch control, reducing pitch safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action for the trim; by the time the resulting attitude/force change is noticed the trim excursion may be advanced, compressing the time available to recover.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An undetected running trim excursion is potentially more severe than an erroneous static setting, but its worst-case aircraft effect depends on trim rate, authority and travel limits and on the phase of manifestation — none of which the AFHA function definition fixes. Cannot bound to a single class without that trim-runaway characterisation; abstaining.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flap actuation — reduced or asymmetric flap deployment relative to the selection
fha.effAc: Flap deploys to less than the selected setting or asymmetrically; asymmetry braking at each flap section limits the asymmetry, so the aircraft flies an approach/landing at a reduced-flap configuration with higher approach speed and lengthened landing distance rather than an uncontrolled roll.
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise the flap disagreement against the selection, adopt the reduced-flap landing procedure and fly a higher-speed approach; workload increases significantly.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A reduced-flap landing raises approach speed and landing distance — a significant reduction in landing safety margin and a significant increase in crew workload — with asymmetry bounded by the section braking. Proposed Major on the stated effects; confirm against the reduced-flap landing performance for the declared landing distances. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch trim authority — reduced range or rate of pitch trim available to the crew
fha.effAc: Reduced trim range or rate leaves the crew unable to fully trim out pitch control forces across the CG and configuration range; the aircraft remains controllable through the primary pitch control and the mechanical reversion path, but sustained out-of-trim forces are carried.
fha.effCrew: Crew hold residual pitch forces manually and manage configuration/CG within the reduced trim envelope; a slight-to-significant increase in workload depending on how much trim authority is lost.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The safety-margin and workload effect scales with how much trim range/rate is lost — a small reduction is a slight workload increase, a large one a significant reduction in pitch safety margins — and the AFHA function definition does not quantify the residual authority. Cannot select one class without that; abstaining rather than defaulting to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric flap actuation — crew aware
fha.effAc: Rolling and yawing moment from unequal flap deflection between sections; asymmetry braking at each flap section limits the divergence, but a residual roll asymmetry degrades handling in the low-speed approach and landing configuration where flap is deployed.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the asymmetry via display annunciation and control-force cues, apply lateral trim/aileron and adjust the approach; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Attitude excursion and possible go-around; no direct injury expected if controllability retained.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Aware asymmetric flap with asymmetry braking limiting divergence: significant reduction in functional capability and significant increase in crew workload in a critical phase, controllability retained — supports Major. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric flap actuation — undetected
fha.effAc: Unequal flap deflection produces an uncorrected rolling/yawing moment; with the crew taking no corrective action the asymmetry persists into the low-speed approach and landing configuration.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding the asymmetry; the uncorrected roll may not be attributed until a large control deviation develops close to the ground.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The magnitude of uncorrected roll authority left by the asymmetry-braking limit, and whether controllability is retained without crew action at low speed, is not stated in the SDD; without that the aircraft effect cannot be bounded and severity cannot be derived. Needs asymmetry-braking authority limit and low-speed controllability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of secondary flight control (flap drive and pitch trim)
fha.effAc: No flap actuation and no powered pitch trim; take-off and landing performed in a non-optimal (clean or fixed) configuration with higher speeds and longer distances against a 760 m paved / 900 m water landing requirement; pitch trim reverts to the mechanical reversion path.
fha.effCrew: Crew fly a flapless/fixed-configuration approach with mechanical pitch trim only; significantly increased workload and reduced margins on the coastal short-field/water case.
fha.effPax: Higher approach and touchdown speeds; occupant risk elevated if runway/water run margin is eroded, but controllability and a mechanical pitch-trim path are retained.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of flap plus powered pitch trim in the landing/take-off case, with only mechanical pitch-trim reversion and no flap, is a large reduction in functional capability and safety margins against the short landing-distance case — supports Hazardous; confirm against demonstrated flapless performance. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary flight indication
fha.effAc: Misleading attitude/air-data on the primary display drives the aircraft toward an unsafe state if acted upon; channel A reads the same primary sensor set, so an erroneous primary source can also corrupt one flight-control channel's data.
fha.effCrew: Continuous cross-comparison against the standby display and channel B (a different air-data source) is annunciated on disagreement rather than voted; crew must detect, identify the failed source and revert to standby — high workload, potential for misleading action before reversion.
fha.effPax: Attitude/flight-path excursion during the interval before the crew reverts to the standby picture.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading primary flight indication, detectable only by crew recognition of an annunciated disagreement (not auto-voted), with the standby source available for reversion: a large reduction in safety margins with excessive crew workload before reversion — supports Hazardous; confirm against the reversion time and any Catastrophic case if the standby is unavailable. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous powertrain-state indication
fha.effAc: The powertrain page shows state of charge, available power from each source, coolant loop temperature and warmest module — on a hybrid the answer to 'how much flying is left in it' is not a fuel gauge; erroneous SOC/available-power indication can lead the crew to misjudge remaining energy and mismanage the sector reserve or the go-around/diversion case.
fha.effCrew: Crew make energy-management decisions on a false picture; may commit to an approach or diversion the true energy state cannot support, or shut down a healthy source; increased workload and potential mis-decision.
fha.effPax: Exposure to a fuel/energy-exhaustion scenario if the false indication is acted on through to a committed diversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The worst-case aircraft outcome depends on whether independent means (turbogenerator vs store dissimilarity, direct source data) let the crew catch an erroneous energy picture, and on the reserve-sizing case, which the SDD states is preliminary and expected to move; without the cross-check credit and the reserve basis the effect cannot be bounded to a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew alerting — the alerting function presents a warning/caution that misrepresents the true system state (false, missing-prioritised or wrongly-prioritised alert), the crew being able to detect via the underlying pages
fha.effAc: Alerting is the single place where discretes and data from every system in §2.2 are prioritised. An erroneous alert can prompt a crew response to a condition that is not occurring, or mask attention from one that is; the underlying flight and powertrain pages remain available for the crew to reconcile against.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to diagnose and cross-check the alert against the flight and powertrain pages; potential for a mistaken procedural response before reconciliation.
fha.effPax: No direct effect unless a mistaken crew response follows.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous alerting from the single prioritisation point drives increased crew workload and a potential mistaken response, but the underlying pages remain available for reconciliation and the alert cannot be inhibited beyond master-caution acknowledgement — effects support a significant increase in crew workload, not a large reduction in safety margins. Engineer to confirm class and whether a false-warning-driven action could be more severe in a specific phase. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary flight indication — undetected: the primary display presents attitude or air data that is wrong and the error is not annunciated, so the crew continue their duties acting on it
fha.effAc: The primary display and channel A share the primary sensor set, rack, route R-5 and electrical channel 1. Cross-comparison against the standby source is continuous and a disagreement is annunciated rather than resolved automatically; an undetected erroneous primary indication implies the misleading picture is presented without the disagreement being raised, so the crew may fly to erroneous attitude/air data.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading primary flight information without a cue to distrust it; recovery depends on independently recognising the standby source disagrees.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to the consequences of the crew flying to erroneous flight information.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary attitude/air data acted on by the crew is a large reduction in safety margins where the annunciated cross-compare that normally bounds this case is, by definition, not raised. Proposed Hazardous; engineer to confirm and to confirm whether the design can present erroneous primary data with the cross-compare truly failing to annunciate. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous powertrain-state indication — undetected: the powertrain page presents state of charge, available power, coolant temperature or warmest-module state that is wrong and unannunciated, so the crew continue their duties acting on it
fha.effAc: The powertrain page shows state of charge, available power from each source, coolant loop temperature and the warmest energy-store module, because on a hybrid aircraft the energy-remaining question is not answered by a fuel gauge. An undetected error in that page means the crew's energy and thermal picture is wrong without a cue to distrust it.
fha.effCrew: Crew plan and commit to the sector on a wrong energy or thermal picture without a cue to reconcile.
fha.effPax: No effect stated by the design absent the aircraft-level consequence.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes the powertrain page as the crew's sole means of judging energy remaining on a hybrid aircraft, but it does not state the aircraft-level consequence of committing to a sector on an undetected-wrong energy/thermal picture (e.g. energy exhaustion short of a diversion, or a thermal event masked). Without that stated effect a severity cannot be derived without guessing. NEEDED: aircraft-level effect of the crew acting on undetected-erroneous powertrain state, and any independent energy/thermal cross-check.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary flight indication: attitude/air data on the primary display is degraded or partially unavailable, the loss being detected
fha.effAc: Loss of one display unit leaves the other presenting the full picture; loss of the primary sensor set leaves the standby display and channel B, which reads it. The standby source is independent across sensor, probe, electrical channel and battery, so a detected partial loss of the primary picture reverts the crew to the standby indication.
fha.effCrew: Crew revert to the remaining display unit or the standby indication; increased workload managing a degraded primary picture on an annunciated reversion.
fha.effPax: No direct effect while the standby picture remains available.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A detected partial loss reverting to an independent standby source is a significant reduction in functional capability / increase in crew workload rather than a large one, given the four-way-independent standby remains. Proposed Major; engineer to confirm and to confirm the worst applicable phase. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of powertrain-state indication: the powertrain page is degraded or partially unavailable (some of SOC, available power, loop temperature or warmest-module state not presented), the loss being detected
fha.effAc: The powertrain page is the crew's means of judging energy remaining and thermal state on a hybrid aircraft. A detected partial loss removes some of that picture while the crew remains aware the information is degraded.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing energy and thermal decisions with a partially available powertrain picture, with awareness that the indication is degraded.
fha.effPax: No direct effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of the crew making energy/thermal decisions on a partially-available powertrain picture (e.g. conservative diversion vs. committing beyond reserves), so a severity cannot be derived without guessing. NEEDED: aircraft-level effect of degraded-but-detected powertrain indication and any procedural/reserve margin that bounds it.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight and powertrain indication
fha.effAc: Loss of the primary presentation of attitude, air data, powertrain state and prioritised crew alerting on both primary display units. The crew reverts to the standby display for attitude and air data; powertrain state (state of charge, available power from each source, coolant loop temperature) and the single prioritised alerting function are unavailable, degrading the crew's ability to manage a hybrid powertrain whose remaining-energy picture is not a fuel gauge.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload: attitude and air-data flying transfers to the single standby instrument, and the crew loses the consolidated alerting that prioritises discretes and data from every system. Loss of powertrain awareness impairs energy management and reversion decisions in IMC at low flight levels.
fha.effPax: No direct effect on occupants beyond that of the resulting degraded operation.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the primary flight, powertrain and consolidated-alerting picture forces the crew onto the standby source alone and removes energy-state awareness on a hybrid aircraft, a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload in IMC. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby attitude indication
fha.effAc: The standby attitude indication presents attitude in error. The primary display presents attitude on a separate sensor set, and continuous cross-comparison between the primary and standby sources annunciates a disagreement rather than resolving it, so the erroneous standby value is detectable against the primary source; flight control channel B also reads this source.
fha.effCrew: Crew is alerted to a standby/primary attitude disagreement and flies the primary attitude source; increased workload to identify the faulty source and to manage the annunciated cross-compare, and reduced confidence in the standby as the independent backup.
fha.effPax: No direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the primary display available and cross-comparison annunciated, an erroneous standby attitude is detected and the crew flies the valid primary source; this is a significant increase in crew workload rather than a loss of a safety-critical picture. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby air-data indication
fha.effAc: The standby air-data indication (from the second probe) presents air data in error. The primary display presents air data on a separate pitot-static and sensor set, and continuous cross-comparison annunciates a standby/primary disagreement; flight control channel B reads the standby air-data source.
fha.effCrew: Crew is alerted to an air-data disagreement and flies the primary air-data source; increased workload to isolate the faulty source and manage a channel-B input that is reading erroneous air data until the source is identified.
fha.effPax: No direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Primary air data remains available and the disagreement is annunciated, so the erroneous standby air data is detected and the crew reverts to the valid source; significant increase in workload, not a loss of a required capability. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby attitude indication — undetected
fha.effAc: The standby attitude indication is in error and the error is not annunciated (cross-compare not triggering or not observed). With the primary display available the crew normally flies the primary attitude source, so an undetected standby error is latent; its consequence becomes safety-critical only in the subsequent case where the primary source is also lost and the crew reverts to a standby that is silently wrong, and channel B is fed erroneous attitude.
fha.effCrew: No immediate crew action, since the standby error is undetected and the crew continue normally on the primary source; the hazard is a latent condition that misleads the crew and channel B if the primary source is later lost.
fha.effPax: No direct effect on occupants in the latent state.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether this reaches Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on whether the standby is credited as the last-resort attitude source when the primary display is lost (misleading last-line source) and on the assumed exposure/latency of an undetected standby error while the primary remains valid — not determinable from the SDD, which states cross-compare annunciates but not the coverage of an undetected standby error; severity left empty pending that engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous standby air-data indication — undetected
fha.effAc: The standby air-data indication is in error and the error is not annunciated. With primary air data available the crew flies the primary source, so the standby error is latent; it becomes consequential in the subsequent case where the primary air-data source is lost and the crew and channel B rely on standby air data that is silently wrong.
fha.effCrew: No immediate crew action while undetected; the crew continue normally on the primary source. The condition is latent and misleads the crew and channel B if the primary air-data source is later lost.
fha.effPax: No direct effect on occupants in the latent state.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — As for the undetected attitude case, severity hinges on crediting the standby as the last-resort air-data source when the primary is lost and on the assumed exposure/latency of an undetected standby air-data error — neither is established by the SDD, which states cross-comparison is annunciated but not the coverage of an undetected standby fault; severity left empty pending engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of gear actuation — one unit fails to extend or lock down
fha.effAc: One gear unit not down-and-locked at touchdown; asymmetric ground contact on a paved landing, or on a water landing an unretracted/partially-extended unit disturbs the hull planing attitude. Mechanical free-fall extension and split-channel power provide alternate means, and two dissimilar sensors per lock indicate the mismatch.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by the gear-position comparison against selected surface; assumed to action free-fall extension and/or divert to the appropriate surface, with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Possible occupant injury in an asymmetric or off-attitude touchdown.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-unit partial loss with free-fall backup and clear indication yields a significant reduction in safety margins and increased crew workload rather than loss of the aircraft; proposed Major for engineer confirmation. Worst phase Landing. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of gear stowage sealing — bay not fully sealed for water operation
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the SF-008 FCIM (SF-008 carries only TL/PL/M), and the SF-008 function definition ('Actuate and stow the landing gear') does not itself state a water-ingress / flotation effect. The SDD notes gear bays are 'sealed against water ingress by their doors and drained above the static waterline', but the hull-flotation consequence of a sealing failure is an HUF/HUA hull-integrity matter not captured by this gear-actuation function — cannot classify without the sealing-failure effect being stated at aircraft level. Needs engineer to confirm whether this condition belongs on SF-008 or on the hull functions.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of gear actuation and stowage — no unit extends or retracts by normal means
fha.effAc: Gear cannot be positioned by the normal electro-mechanical means. Mechanical free-fall extension remains as the independent last resort to reach a down-and-locked land configuration; a gear stuck extended for a water landing, or unable to extend for a paved landing, forces reversion to the alternate surface. No hydraulic system exists, so free-fall is the sole non-electrical path.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to loss of normal actuation; assumed to select free-fall extension and to choose the surface the resulting configuration supports, with high workload and reduced options.
fha.effPax: Occupant injury possible in a gear-up or gear-inappropriate touchdown.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of normal gear actuation across all units, mitigated only by mechanical free-fall and constrained by the amphibian surface-selection dependency, gives a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload; proposed Hazardous for confirmation. If the free-fall path is credited independent, this may reduce — engineer to disposition. Worst phase Landing. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear-configuration indication — displayed configuration does not match the true gear state
fha.effAc: Crew may configure for the wrong surface based on false indication: a gear-up landing on a paved strip, or a gear-down water landing that can upset the hull. On an amphibian a wrong-surface touchdown is the dominant hazard. Two dissimilar sensors per lock and a comparison against selected surface exist to reduce single-sensor error, but an erroneous displayed result defeats that check for the crew.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on false configuration information; the mismatch alert against selected surface is the primary defence, and its own failure to reflect truth drives the effect.
fha.effPax: Serious occupant injury possible in a wrong-surface landing.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading gear-configuration indication that could lead to a wrong-surface landing on an amphibian gives a large reduction in safety margins; proposed Hazardous pending engineer confirmation of whether the two-dissimilar-sensor comparison is credited to preclude the fully-misleading case. Worst phase Landing. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous configuration-versus-surface comparison — mismatch alert fails to annunciate or falsely annunciates
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the SF-009 FCIM (SF-009 carries SF-009-M, not an M2). The SF-009 function 'Indicate gear configuration against selected surface' supports a comparison-alert failure conceptually, but its aircraft effect overlaps SF-009-M (erroneous indication) unless the specific failure — sensors correct, comparison logic wrong, or surface-selection input wrong — is stated. Cannot classify without that distinct effect being defined at aircraft level; needs engineer to confirm whether M2 is a distinct condition or a duplicate of SF-009-M.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous configuration-versus-surface comparison, crew unaware — the comparison of gear position against the selected landing surface is wrong and no mismatch is annunciated when one exists
fha.effAc: The single function that catches a wrong configuration for the surface fails silently, so a genuine gear/surface mismatch proceeds to touchdown unannounced (gear-up on paved, gear-down on water).
fha.effCrew: Crew are not alerted to a mismatch and continue the approach on the assumption the configuration is correct; the comparison is the design's primary defence and it is absent.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a mis-configured landing without warning.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The effect is loss of the mismatch alert with an undetected wrong-surface touchdown, but the SDD does not bound the resulting touchdown consequence (structural damage vs loss of aircraft/occupant injury); that outcome input is needed before a class can be committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded water-rudder deflection — water rudder deflects without or contrary to crew command
fha.effAc: Unwanted yawing/steering input during water operations; the rudder should be retracted for take-off and landing, so an uncommanded deflection at those points, or an unwanted swing during taxi, degrades directional control on the water. Reversion to differential thrust is available if the actuator is released.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload to counter the unwanted deflection with pedals/thrust and, if needed, to invoke the manual release; directional control on the water reverts to differential thrust.
fha.effPax: Occupants subjected to an uncommanded swing during water manoeuvring.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects range from a minor handling upset during taxi to a directional-control disturbance during a high-energy water take-off/landing, but the SDD does not bound the water-phase directional-control consequence (deviation, hull loading, capsize risk); that water-handling input is needed before a class can be committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent water-rudder deployment (uncommanded deflection to deployed position)
fha.effAc: Water rudder is retracted for take-off, landing and all land operations by design; an uncommanded deployment presents a submerged/extended blade at planing speeds or on land. The SDD does not state the aerodynamic/hydrodynamic or structural effect of a deployed blade at take-off/landing speed, so the aircraft effect cannot be fully bounded from the design description.
fha.effCrew: Position is annunciated (§5.13.6) and a hardwired interlock retracts the rudder on gear-down (§5.13.2), so the crew has indication and a re-selection/interlock path.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states the rudder is retracted for take-off/landing and land ops but does not state the effect of an uncommanded deployed blade at planing/landing speed (directional upset, drag asymmetry or blade/sternpost structural loading). Need the deployed-at-speed effect (structural substantiation / handling) to derive a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and overheat detection — one detection zone or one loop degraded, detection still available in the remaining zones/loops
fha.effAc: One designated fire zone (store bay, generator compartment or a nacelle) loses full detection coverage; a fire or overheat originating there may be detected late or not at all, while the other zones remain protected. A single loop fault is annunciated as a fault, not a warning.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to a loop/zone fault by the alerting function; increased monitoring of the affected zone and dispatch/continuation decision required.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect unless an undetected event develops in the affected zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A partial loss leaves detection available in the remaining zones/loops with the fault annunciated, so it is a significant reduction in the safety margin of the fire-protection function with increased crew monitoring — not a full loss of protection. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection (crew aware) — no detection in any fire zone, annunciated to the crew
fha.effAc: No detection of fire, overheat or thermal-runaway in any designated fire zone (store bay, generator compartment, both nacelles) or the cabin; a developing event proceeds without the automatic warning, isolation and containment triggers that depend on detection.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of the loss of detection; heightened workload and a curtailment/diversion decision, but they cannot substitute for zone detection in flight.
fha.effPax: Exposed to an undetected in-flight fire event until it manifests by other cues.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of detection across all fire zones removes the primary trigger for isolation, containment and extinguishant on an aircraft carrying a high-voltage energy store with runaway potential; a large reduction in the fire-protection safety margin. Awareness lets the crew curtail but not restore protection, holding it below Catastrophic. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of fire and overheat detection (crew unaware) — detection failed with no annunciation, crew continue normal duties
fha.effAc: Detection is lost with no fault indication; a subsequent fire, overheat or thermal-runaway in any fire zone — including the high-voltage store bay — proceeds with no warning and no automatic isolation/containment trigger, and the first cue is the developed event itself.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware, continue normal duties and take no action; no opportunity to pre-empt or curtail before the event manifests.
fha.effPax: Exposed to an undetected, unmitigated in-flight fire developing without warning.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With detection latently lost and the crew unaware, a store-bay thermal-runaway or nacelle/generator fire develops without the warning, isolation, containment or extinguishant response that all depend on detection, with no crew opportunity to intervene — a plausible loss-of-airplane path. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge — the single generator-compartment bottle discharges with no fire present
fha.effAc: The single generator-compartment extinguishant bottle discharges when no fire exists, depleting the only suppression reserve on the aircraft; a subsequent genuine generator fire cannot be extinguished. Discharge itself does not directly affect flight path.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the discharge; must account for loss of the suppression capability and adjust the dispatch/continuation decision.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect from the discharge event itself.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An inadvertent discharge expends the sole, non-reserved suppression bottle, leaving a subsequent generator fire without extinguishant — a significant reduction in the fire-protection safety margin. Isolation (fuel shutoff, contactor-open, feather) remains available as the designed primary response, holding it below Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent isolation of a healthy source — an uncommanded isolation/shutoff (fuel shutoff, propulsion-bus or string contactor-open) acts on a source with no fire or thermal event present
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the SF-012 FCIM (the malfunction cells there are inadvertent extinguishant discharge and undetected failure to isolate/discharge). Grounding the aircraft effect requires confirming which isolation output erroneously actuates (turbogenerator fuel shutoff, propulsion-bus contactor, or store string contactor per §5.15.4) and its consequence on thrust/energy availability; without that the effects and severity cannot be stated. Needs a confirmed FCIM condition before classification.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure of the fire and thermal protection function to isolate or discharge on demand — a fire, overheat or thermal-runaway event occurs and the isolation (fuel shutoff, bus contactor open, feather) or extinguishant response does not act, with the crew unaware the response has failed
fha.effAc: An in-progress fire/overheat/thermal event in a designated fire zone (store bay, generator compartment, nacelle) is not contained, isolated or extinguished; because the failure of the response is undetected the crew take no compensating action, so the event is free to propagate along the zone and its routings until it reaches structure, high-voltage runs, fuel or an occupied compartment
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties; no warning of the failed response; first cue is the physical progression of the fire itself, by which point compensating action may be ineffective
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected failure to arrest an active fire/thermal event in a fire zone permits uncontrolled propagation toward fuel, HV runs and occupied compartments with no crew intervention, consistent with loss of the airplane [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of the fire and thermal protection function — containment, isolation or extinguishing is available in some zones or responses but degraded or unavailable in others (e.g. one detection loop or one response path lost)
fha.effAc: Reduced ability to contain, isolate or extinguish an event; for a given zone the aircraft may retain detection but lose a response, or retain one response path of a redundant pair, reducing the margin against an uncontained event
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The effect depends on WHICH capability is lost in WHICH zone (store-bay containment vs generator-bay extinguishant vs nacelle isolation are different in kind per the SDD), and no single aircraft-level effect is stated by the function definition alone; the specific degraded configuration and its residual protection are needed before an effect and severity can be derived. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of the fire and thermal protection function — no containment, no isolation and no extinguishing available in any zone, with detection also lost
fha.effAc: No means to detect, contain, isolate or extinguish a fire, overheat or thermal-runaway event anywhere on the aircraft; should such an event occur it is free to propagate toward fuel, high-voltage runs and occupied compartments
fha.effCrew: No fire/overheat warning; crew cannot command isolation or discharge
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss of the protection function is dangerous only in combination with an initiating fire/thermal event; the standalone loss is a latent condition whose aircraft-level severity depends on the assumed coincident event and exposure, which the function definition does not establish — provide the event/exposure basis before classifying. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin pressure control — the cabin environment function schedules or holds cabin pressure incorrectly (e.g. outflow valve driven to a wrong position), producing a cabin altitude different from that commanded, with the error annunciated/apparent to the crew
fha.effAc: Cabin altitude departs from schedule while the aircraft continues to fly; an independent positive-pressure relief valve and a manual outflow-valve override are provided per the SDD, and the maximum operating altitude is FL120
fha.effCrew: Crew observe cabin pressure/differential indication, action the manual outflow-valve override, and manage the cabin altitude; increased workload
fha.effPax: Discomfort from off-schedule cabin altitude; below the physiological thresholds bounded by an FL120 ceiling
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An annunciated erroneous pressure schedule with an independent relief valve, a manual override and an FL120 ceiling yields a significant increase in crew workload and occupant discomfort rather than incapacitation; confirm against the certified cabin-altitude schedule [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent cabin depressurisation — the cabin environment function loses pressurisation without command (e.g. outflow valve fails open) so cabin altitude rises toward aircraft altitude
fha.effAc: Cabin depressurises toward ambient; per the SDD the aircraft is designed to operate unpressurised on stored energy alone and the maximum operating altitude is FL120, so the exposure is bounded by that ceiling; crew initiate a descent to a lower altitude
fha.effCrew: Crew recognise the depressurisation from cabin-altitude indication, don't-lose-control workload increase, initiate descent to a habitable altitude
fha.effPax: Physical distress from rapid cabin-altitude increase; severity of hypoxia exposure bounded by the FL120 ceiling and the time-to-descend
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded without the certified cabin-altitude schedule, the time-of-useful-consciousness at the operating ceiling and whether descent to a habitable altitude is always achievable within that time; the FL120 ceiling and the by-design unpressurised reversion suggest a bounded effect but the physiological margin is not established by the provided inputs. NOTE: SF-013-M2 has no anchoring FCIM row in the current model — add one before committing this classification. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of cabin pressure schedule
fha.effAc: Cabin pressure control operates to a wrong schedule with no annunciation; the outflow/relief arrangement continues but at an incorrect cabin altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action, having no cue that the schedule is wrong.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states the pressure-control function and its single outflow valve with independent relief, and an FL120 ceiling, but gives no cabin-altitude schedule, exposure limits or physiological effect at the operating envelope. An occupant effect and thus a severity require a cabin-altitude/exposure judgement not present in the provided inputs.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of cabin conditioning and pressurisation
fha.effAc: Conditioning and pressurisation degraded but not lost; the aircraft remains within its FL120 envelope where the unpressurised case is a declared operating condition.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload managing cabin conditions and monitoring cabin altitude; degradation annunciated.
fha.effPax: Reduced cabin comfort; physical discomfort possible depending on residual pressurisation.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: From the stated effects: with a FL120 ceiling under which flying unpressurised is a designed operating condition, a partial degradation yields a slight increase in crew workload and passenger discomfort rather than a safety-margin reduction. Severity PROPOSED for confirmation. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of pressurisation with ventilation retained
fha.effAc: Aircraft is ventilated but not pressurised — the described reversion state when flying on stored energy with the generator shut down; consistent with the FL120 operating envelope.
fha.effCrew: Reversion annunciated as a change of state rather than a failure; crew operate to the unpressurised operating condition.
fha.effPax: Cabin ventilated and heated; no pressurisation, tolerable within the FL120 envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The SDD states this is a designed operating condition, not an emergency, at a ceiling chosen to make it so; effects are at most a slight increase in crew workload/passenger discomfort. Severity PROPOSED — confirm whether this is a failure condition at all or the normal reversion. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin conditioning and pressurisation
fha.effAc: No conditioning and no pressurisation; aircraft must be operated within the FL120 envelope where the unpressurised case is a declared operating condition, with no ventilation/heating alternative available.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload managing an unconditioned, unpressurised cabin; loss annunciated.
fha.effPax: Loss of conditioning and pressurisation; discomfort and, absent the electrical ventilation/heating path, degraded cabin environment across the sector.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: From the stated effects: unlike the ventilation-retained case, complete loss removes the electrical recirculation/heating reversion as well, giving a significant increase in crew workload and passenger physical distress; bounded below Hazardous by the FL120 ceiling that makes the unpressurised case an operating condition. Severity PROPOSED for confirmation. [anchor MAJ-3 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of windscreen clearing
fha.effAc: Reduced windscreen anti-fog capability; forward visibility through part of the windscreen degraded, with the bleed and electric-backup paths only partially effective.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload maintaining visual reference, most significant during water/paved approach and landing where external cues are needed.
fha.effPax: No direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: From the stated effects: partial degradation of anti-fog, with a bleed-plus-electric-backup arrangement, yields a slight increase in crew workload and slight reduction in external visual reference rather than loss of it. Severity PROPOSED for confirmation; a full clearing-loss case is covered by another condition. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of windscreen clearing
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided functions/SDD describe windscreen clearing as a bleed-fed anti-fog function with an electric backup element but do not state the aircraft-level effect of a complete loss of forward external visibility across the applicable phases; without a grounded effect on aircraft, crew and occupants the severity cannot be derived. Needs engineering judgement on the loss-of-forward-vision effect (degree of impairment, availability of side windows/instrument approach, worst applicable phase).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary control commanding — channel B ceases to command part of its surface set while channel A remains available
fha.effAc: Loss of channel B's commanding to part of its surface set leaves the remaining half of the affected pair driven by channel A; the SDD states the surfaces are sized so one half of each pair is sufficient, so the aircraft remains controllable at reduced control redundancy — the second channel is now the sole path for the affected surface(s)
fha.effCrew: Loss is detected and annunciated (partial-loss, crew-aware); crew acknowledge the degraded state and continue with reduced redundancy per procedure — increased monitoring workload
fha.effPax: No direct effect expected in the degraded state
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detected partial loss of one channel's commanding removes a layer of the dual-channel redundancy but the SDD states each channel alone can fly the aircraft through its half of each surface pair, so this is a significant reduction in safety margins / functional capability at aircraft level with an aware, procedurally-managed crew response — MAJ-1. Severity PROPOSED; confirm the annunciation and residual authority assumptions. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary control commanding — channel B loses all commanding of its surface set
fha.effAc: Complete loss of channel B commanding transfers control to channel A, which the SDD states is alone sufficient to fly the aircraft; the aircraft continues on a single primary flight-control channel with the mechanical reversion path (pitch trim and lower rudder segment) remaining below that — no aircraft-level loss of control from this single-channel loss, but the aircraft is now single-thread on primary control
fha.effCrew: Detected and annunciated; automatic transfer to channel A, crew confirm the degraded single-channel state and continue per procedure with heightened vigilance for a subsequent channel-A failure
fha.effPax: No direct effect expected on transfer to the healthy channel
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With automatic annunciated transfer to channel A — which the SDD states is alone sufficient — this single-channel total loss is a significant reduction in safety margins/functional capability (loss of one of two independent primary control channels), consistent with MAJ-1, not Hazardous, because full primary control commanding remains on the surviving channel. Severity PROPOSED; confirm automatic-transfer coverage across all phases. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear-configuration indication, crew unaware — indication shows a locked/correct configuration that does not match the true gear state
fha.effAc: Aircraft configured wrong for the landing surface without a valid cue: gear may be up for a paved landing or down for a water landing, and the indication that would prompt correction is itself erroneous. On an amphibian a config/surface mismatch at touchdown risks hull/gear damage or capsize.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on a false-correct indication and take no corrective action; the erroneous state is only discoverable, if at all, from external cues at low height.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a mis-configured landing (nose-over on water or gear-up on paved).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point toward the severe end (undetected wrong-surface landing), but the SDD does not quantify the touchdown outcome (hull damage vs loss of aircraft, occupant injury) needed to distinguish HAZ-3/HAZ-1 from CAT-1; a landing-outcome/structural input is required before committing a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of gear-configuration indication — one unit's indication unavailable, remaining units indicated
fha.effAc: Configuration status for one gear unit is unavailable; the crew cannot confirm that unit is in the correct/locked state for the surface, though the other two units remain indicated.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to confirm configuration by other means (mechanical free-fall confirmation, procedure) and reduced certainty on one unit before committing to touchdown.
fha.effPax: Passengers minimally affected pending crew resolution.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8).
